finding: The deferred-wait graph has no executable XRT dependency, memory-order, progress, or failure-propagation protocol. `start()` submission order is not defined here as a completion dependency; under polling-gate reading, a producer fault never publishes the required version, so a dependent wrapper can wait forever and epoch commit can never collect all statuses or report the first error. This is the exact explicit-failure/order obstacle the candidate claims to solve, so adding an abort/dependency scheduler would be an obstacle-level redesign rather than a coherence wording patch.
why_not_repaired: The candidate's branch-(i) audit declares correct ordering, delayed errors, and first-fault commit to be the load-bearing obstacle. Supplying a host event DAG, ERT dependency mechanism, or device abort/progress protocol changes the actual execution mechanism and cannot be patched around by skipping dependent nodes or waiting per call.
verbatim_step_quote:
5. Add receipt checks and tensor-version gates to each finite wrapper; inputs are R_i, descriptor BO, and device version table, and outputs are either the new output-tensor versions consumed by downstream operators or a first-fault status code.
6. Replace per-call waits with graph-ordered asynchronous submissions and retain every descriptor BO, run handle, and tensor allocation until epoch resolution; inputs are admitted calls and dependency versions, and output is an in-flight epoch whose downstream nodes consume only published producer versions.
8. Implement epoch commit at graph return and at unchanged explicit synchronize/copy/read boundaries; inputs are all run statuses and provisional versions, and output is either atomically committed tensors/state returned to llama.cpp or an explicit first error with provisional state discarded.
executed_evidence: UNEXECUTED (no execution tool available), self-contained trace: let producer N0 require one run and publish tensor version v=8 only on success; let downstream N1's wrapper gate on input v=8. Submit start(N0), then start(N1), then make N0 return Fault(0) without publishing v=8. The stated outputs permit N0 to emit a fault status, but no step publishes an abort/failure version consumed by N1. N1's gate therefore remains false forever. Step 8 requires statuses from all runs, including N1, so it cannot terminate or report Fault(0). Independently, if publication is a device-memory write, the text supplies no release-before-version/acquire-after-version rule, so observing v=8 does not as written establish visibility of N0's tensor bytes. These failures hold whether `gate` means polling (missing abort/progress/memory order) or XRT dependency (no dependency artifact is produced or consumed).

finding: Mutable KV alias correctness consumes an alias relation that no prior step produces. Tensor IDs/versions and a read/write-set label do not identify overlapping storage intervals or redirect every view to a provisional COW page, so a downstream alias can observe committed bytes or wait on the wrong version even though the writer published its provisional tensor version. This is the candidate's declared mutable-KV obstacle and cannot be repaired by abstaining on aliases.
why_not_repaired: A sound fix requires a canonical storage-object/byte-range/view model, overlap-aware versioning, descriptor rebinding, and page commit rules across all GGML aliases. That is load-bearing mechanism design for the exact aliasing obstacle in BLOCK 2, not narrative alignment.
verbatim_step_quote:
2. Extend the support-query path to emit R_i records keyed by graph invocation and node index; inputs are the real node signature, backend tensor metadata, support-predicate version, and loaded xclbin/kernel metadata, and output is an immutable receipt table or an explicit unsupported result.
7. Route KV-cache and other mutable writes to provisional copy-on-write pages and resolve aliases through the epoch version map; inputs are committed state and node write sets, and output is staged state read by later attention operations without changing generated logits before commit.
executed_evidence: UNEXECUTED (no execution tool available), self-contained trace: committed storage page P at version 7 contains [0,0,0,0]. Tensor A and view tensor V have distinct tensor IDs but both denote P[0:4]. N0 writes through A and stages provisional P version 8 as [1,2,3,4]. N1 reads through V and should compute 1+2+3+4=10. R_i records tensor IDs/versions and read/write sets, but no produced artifact states A and V share canonical page P and byte interval [0,4). Publishing A/P:8 therefore neither necessarily advances V's version nor rebinds V's descriptor to provisional P:8. N1 either reads committed V:7 and computes 0, an error of 10, or waits forever for a V-specific version 8. All-identical alias views amplify the same failure; no threshold or empirical outcome resolves the missing dataflow artifact.
